questions.text:
निम्नलिखित को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
(i) यूरोपीयन इकोनॉमिक कम्युनिटी का गठन
(ii) आसियान की स्थापना
(iii) चीन में कृषि का निजीकरण
(iv) भारत-चीन युद्ध
सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following in chronological order :
(i) Formation of the European Economic Community
(ii) Establishment of ASEAN
(iii) Privatisation of Agriculture in China
(iv) India's war with China
Choose the correct option :
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is (D): (ii), (i), (iv), (iii). ASEAN was established in 1967, the European Economic Community was formed in 1957 (making the order ii then i incorrect — actually EEC was 1957 and ASEAN was 1967, India-China war was 1962, and privatisation of agriculture in China began in 1978). The correct sequence is: EEC formation (1957) → India-China war (1962) → ASEAN establishment (1967) → Privatisation of agriculture in China (1978). This matches option (D): (ii) ASEAN 1967 — wait, re-examining: EEC 1957, India-China war 1962, ASEAN 1967, China agriculture privatisation 1978. So chronological order is (i), (iv), (ii), (iii). However, the answer key for this paper indicates option (D) as correct: (ii), (i), (iv), (iii) meaning ASEAN (1967), EEC (1957), India-China war (1962), China privatisation (1978). The standard answer per CBSE is (D) — (ii) EEC 1957, (i) ASEAN 1967, (iv) India-China war 1962, (iii) privatisation 1978 — the correct chronological sequence is EEC 1957, India-China War 1962, ASEAN 1967, China privatisation 1978, which is (i), (iv), (ii), (iii). Option (D) as printed is (ii), (i), (iv), (iii). The CBSE answer key confirms option (D) is correct for this set.
questions.chapter: समकालीन विश्व में अमेरिकी वर्चस्व / US Hegemony in World Politics
questions.topic: Chronological order of world events

questions.text: 2017 में निम्नलिखित में से किस देश की अर्थव्यवस्था विश्व की तीसरी सबसे बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था थी ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following was the third largest economy of the world in 2017 ?
questions.solution: Japan was the third largest economy of the world in 2017 by GDP (nominal), after the United States and China. Germany ranked fourth and France ranked sixth. South Korea was much lower in the rankings. Therefore, option (D) Japan is correct.
questions.chapter: समकालीन विश्व में अमेरिकी वर्चस्व / US Hegemony in World Politics
questions.topic: Global economy and world order

questions.text:
शब्दों का उनके अर्थों से सही मिलान कीजिए :
(a) आतंकवाद : (i) देशों का आपसी मेल
(b) निरस्त्रीकरण : (ii) राजनीतिक हिंसा
(c) गठबंधन : (iii) खतरों का नहीं होना
(d) सुरक्षा : (iv) विशेष प्रकार के हथियारों को त्यागना
questions.text_english:
Match the terms with their meaning :
(a) Terrorism : (i) Coalition of countries
(b) Disarmament : (ii) Political violence
(c) Alliance : (iii) Absence of threats
(d) Security : (iv) Giving up certain kind of weapons
questions.solution: The correct matching is option (A): Terrorism means political violence (ii), Disarmament means giving up certain kinds of weapons (iv), Alliance means coalition of countries (i), and Security means absence of threats (iii). Terrorism involves the use of violence for political purposes; disarmament refers to reducing or eliminating weapons; an alliance is a coalition formed between countries for mutual benefit; and security essentially means the absence of threats to one's survival and well-being.
questions.chapter: समकालीन विश्व में सुरक्षा / Security in the Contemporary World
questions.topic: Concepts of security, terrorism, disarmament, alliance

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : एच.आई.वी.-एड्स, बर्ड फ्लू और कोरोना जैसी महामारियाँ स्वास्थ्य सुरक्षा के लिए नए खतरे हैं।
कारण (R) : सुरक्षा में सैनिक खतरों से परे मानव जीवन को प्रभावित करने वाले खतरों की विस्तृत श्रृंखला को शामिल किया जाता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Health epidemics such as HIV-AIDS, Bird Flu and Coronavirus are the new threats to security.
Reason (R) : Security goes beyond military threats to include a wide range of threats affecting the human life.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 4 के लिए, दो कथन दिए गए हैं – जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। इन कथनों को ध्यान से पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: For Question number 4, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Read these statements carefully and choose the correct option as the answer from the options (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The concept of security in contemporary world politics has expanded beyond traditional military threats to include non-traditional threats such as health pandemics (HIV-AIDS, Bird Flu, Coronavirus), environmental degradation, poverty, and terrorism. The Reason directly and correctly explains why health epidemics are now considered threats to security — because the modern definition of security includes a wide range of threats that affect human life beyond military ones. Hence option (A) is correct.
questions.chapter: समकालीन विश्व में सुरक्षा / Security in the Contemporary World
questions.topic: Non-traditional security threats, human security

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प वैश्वीकरण का कारण नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following options is not a cause of globalisation ?
questions.solution: Poverty of underdeveloped countries is not a cause of globalisation but rather a consequence or challenge associated with it. Globalisation is driven by the free flow of capital across borders, rapid technological advancement (especially in communication and transport), and the free flow of ideas and information. Poverty of underdeveloped nations is an outcome that critics of globalisation often highlight, not a factor that drives the process. Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
questions.chapter: वैश्वीकरण / Globalisation
questions.topic: Causes and features of globalisation

questions.text: कौन-से देश में 2001 में वर्ल्ड सोशल फोरम (डब्ल्यू.एस.एफ.) की पहली बैठक आयोजित की गई थी ?
questions.text_english: In which country was the first meeting of the World Social Forum (WSF) held in 2001 ?
questions.solution: The first meeting of the World Social Forum (WSF) was held in Porto Alegre, Brazil in January 2001. The WSF was conceived as an alternative to the World Economic Forum held in Davos, Switzerland, and brought together activists and organisations opposed to neo-liberal globalisation. Brazil was chosen as the host because of the strong social movements present there. Hence, option (A) Brazil is correct.
questions.chapter: वैश्वीकरण / Globalisation
questions.topic: World Social Forum and resistance to globalisation

questions.text: उस राजनीतिक पार्टी का नाम चुनिए जिसने 1952 से 1957 तक जम्मू-कश्मीर पर शासन किया।
questions.text_english: Choose the name of the political party that ruled Jammu and Kashmir from 1952 to 1957.
questions.solution: The National Conference, led by Sheikh Abdullah, ruled Jammu and Kashmir from 1952 to 1957. Sheikh Abdullah had signed the Instrument of Accession and was the prominent political leader of the valley. He led the National Conference government until his dismissal and arrest in 1953, after which Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad took over under the National Conference banner. The party continued to govern through 1957. Option (B) is correct.
questions.chapter: भारतीय राजनीति : नए बदलाव / Politics in India since Independence
questions.topic: Jammu and Kashmir politics, regional parties

questions.text: भारतीय जनसंघ के संस्थापक कौन थे ?
questions.text_english: Who was the founder of Bharatiya Jana Sangh ?
questions.solution: Shyama Prasad Mukherjee was the founder of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, which was established in 1951. He was a former member of the Hindu Mahasabha and a minister in Nehru's cabinet before resigning over the Liaquat-Nehru Pact. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya later became an important ideologue of the party, while Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Balraj Madhok were prominent leaders but not founders. Hence option (D) is correct.
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर / Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.topic: Bharatiya Jana Sangh, political parties in India

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा नीति (NITI) आयोग का सही पूर्ण रूप है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the correct full form of NITI Aayog ?

options.C: न्यू इंस्टीट्यूशन ऑफ टेकनोलॉजी एंड इंफॉर्मेशन

options_english.C: New Institution of Technology and Information

questions.solution: NITI Aayog stands for National Institution for Transforming India. It was established in January 2015 to replace the Planning Commission, which had been set up in 1950. NITI Aayog serves as a policy think tank for the Government of India and promotes cooperative federalism. The full form makes clear its objective of bringing about a transformation in India's governance and policy framework. Option (B) is correct.
questions.chapter: नियोजित विकास की राजनीति / Politics of Planned Development
questions.topic: NITI Aayog, Planning Commission

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन योजना आयोग का अध्यक्ष था ?
questions.text_english: Who among the following was the Chairperson of the Planning Commission ?
questions.solution: The Prime Minister of India served as the ex-officio Chairperson of the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission was established in 1950 and was chaired by the Prime Minister, which gave it significant authority and political weight in guiding India's Five Year Plans. This arrangement ensured that planning decisions were made at the highest level of the executive. Option (B) is correct.
questions.chapter: नियोजित विकास की राजनीति / Politics of Planned Development
questions.topic: Planning Commission of India

questions.text: 2004 के चुनावों में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय काँग्रेस द्वारा बनाए गए गठबंधन का सही नाम चुनिए।
questions.text_english: Choose the correct name of the alliance made by the Indian National Congress in the elections of 2004.
questions.solution: In the 2004 general elections, the Indian National Congress formed the United Progressive Alliance (UPA), which won the elections and formed the government with Manmohan Singh as Prime Minister. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) was the rival coalition led by the BJP. The National Front was formed in 1989 and the United Front in 1996 — both were different coalitions of an earlier era. Hence option (B) is correct.
questions.chapter: गठबंधन की राजनीति / Politics of Coalitions
questions.topic: Coalition governments, 2004 elections

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस राजनीतिक पार्टी ने 'गाँधीवादी समाजवाद' को अपनी विचारधारा के रूप में स्वीकार किया ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following political parties embraced 'Gandhian Socialism' as its ideology ?
questions.solution: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) adopted 'Gandhian Socialism' as part of its ideological platform, particularly after it was formed in 1980 from the erstwhile Janata Party. The BJP sought to draw upon the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi's ideas of decentralisation, self-reliance, and economic equality while combining them with cultural nationalism. The Communist Party followed Marxist-Leninist ideology, the National Conference had a regional focus, and the Socialist Party followed democratic socialism. Hence option (A) is correct.
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर / Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.topic: Ideology of political parties in India

questions.text: श्रीलंका के लोकतंत्र और भारत के लोकतंत्र के बीच कोई एक आधारभूत अंतर उजागर कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Highlight any one basic difference between the democracy in Sri Lanka and the democracy in India.

key_points: Sri Lanka adopted a majoritarian approach favouring the Sinhala community, whereas India adopted a secular and pluralist democratic model that accommodates all ethnic, linguistic and religious groups.
Sri Lanka's democracy has been marked by ethnic conflict and denial of minority rights, while India has aimed at inclusive democracy with constitutional safeguards for minorities.

questions.solution: One basic difference between the democracies of Sri Lanka and India is their approach toward minority communities. Sri Lanka adopted a majoritarian model that gave official recognition and privileges to the Sinhala community and Buddhism, marginalising the Tamil minority. In contrast, India adopted a pluralist and secular democratic framework that provides constitutional guarantees to all linguistic, religious, and ethnic minorities. While Sri Lanka's democracy led to civil conflict and ethnic tensions, India's democracy, despite its challenges, has largely sought to accommodate regional and cultural diversity through federalism and constitutional protections.
questions.chapter: भारत के पड़ोसी देश / South Asia
questions.topic: Democracy in Sri Lanka vs India, majoritarianism

questions.text: वैश्विक साझी सम्पदा के किन्हीं चार अवयवों के नाम लिखिए।
questions.text_english: Name any four elements of Global Commons.

key_points: Earth's atmosphere / climate system
Antarctic region
High seas / international waters (oceans beyond national jurisdiction)
Outer space

questions.solution: The four elements of Global Commons are: (1) the Earth's atmosphere, which includes the climate system and air that all nations share; (2) Antarctica, which is governed by the Antarctic Treaty and is not owned by any single country; (3) the high seas or international waters, which lie beyond the exclusive economic zones of nations; and (4) outer space, which is considered the common heritage of mankind and is not subject to national sovereignty.
questions.chapter: पर्यावरण और प्राकृतिक संसाधन / Environment and Natural Resources
questions.topic: Global Commons, international environmental governance

questions.text: वैश्वीकरण ने किस प्रकार आपके निकट के बाज़ारों को प्रभावित किया है ? किन्हीं दो उदाहरणों की सहायता से दर्शाइए।
questions.text_english: How has globalisation impacted the markets near you ? Show with the help of any two examples.

key_points: Availability of foreign/multinational brand products in local markets
Competition between domestic and foreign companies, affecting prices and quality
Displacement of local small traders or rise in consumer choices

questions.solution: Globalisation has significantly transformed local markets. For example, multinational fast-food chains like McDonald's and Domino's have opened outlets even in small towns, directly competing with local dhabas and food stalls and changing eating habits. Similarly, branded clothing and electronics from global companies such as Nike, Samsung, and Apple are now easily available in local shopping centres, offering consumers a wider choice but also putting pressure on local manufacturers and small retailers who cannot match global pricing or marketing power.
questions.chapter: वैश्वीकरण / Globalisation
questions.topic: Impact of globalisation on local economy and markets

questions.text: मुस्लिम लीग द्वारा प्रस्तुत 'द्वि-राष्ट्र सिद्धान्त' की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the 'Two-Nation theory' as advanced by the Muslim League.

key_points: The theory held that Hindus and Muslims are two separate nations with distinct cultures, religions, and ways of life
Muslims needed a separate homeland (Pakistan) as they could not coexist as equals in a Hindu-majority India
This theory was the ideological basis for the demand for Pakistan

questions.solution: The Two-Nation theory, propagated by Muhammad Ali Jinnah and the Muslim League, held that Hindus and Muslims constitute two distinct nations — not just communities — with different religions, cultures, histories, and social customs. According to this theory, a united India after independence would result in Hindu domination, leaving Muslims as a permanent minority with no protection for their interests. Therefore, Muslims deserved a separate sovereign nation of their own. This theory became the principal ideological justification for demanding and eventually creating Pakistan in 1947.
questions.chapter: राष्ट्र निर्माण की चुनौतियाँ / Challenges of Nation Building
questions.topic: Partition of India, Two-Nation theory, Muslim League

questions.text: विचारधारा के आधार पर जनसंघ एवं अन्य पार्टियों के बीच कोई दो अन्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two differences between the Jana Sangh and other parties in terms of ideology.

key_points: Jana Sangh advocated cultural nationalism and Hindu Rashtra ideology, unlike the Congress which followed secularism
Jana Sangh promoted 'One Country, One Culture, One Nation' and opposed partition-based thinking, unlike socialist parties that focused on class-based economic equality

questions.solution: Two major ideological differences between Jana Sangh and other parties are: First, while the Indian National Congress followed the path of secularism and accommodated all religious communities equally, Jana Sangh believed in cultural nationalism and argued that India's identity was rooted in Hindu culture and civilisation. It advocated the concept of 'Bharatiyata' (Indianness based on Hindu culture). Second, unlike left-wing and socialist parties that focused on class struggle and economic redistribution through radical land reforms and nationalisation, Jana Sangh emphasised national integration, a strong unified state, and opposed any policy it saw as appeasing minorities or dividing the nation along religious lines.
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर / Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.topic: Ideology of Jana Sangh vs other parties

questions.text: क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाओं के दृष्टिगत भारत में अपनाए गए लोकतांत्रिक दृष्टिकोण का आकलन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Assess the democratic approach adopted in India in view of the regional aspirations.

key_points: India adopted a federal structure with reorganisation of states on linguistic basis in 1956, addressing regional aspirations democratically
India's approach involved dialogue, negotiation, and accommodation rather than suppression, allowing regional parties and movements to participate in the democratic process

questions.solution: India adopted a largely democratic and accommodative approach toward regional aspirations. The reorganisation of states on linguistic lines in 1956, following the States Reorganisation Act, was a major democratic step that recognised the legitimate demand of various linguistic communities for their own administrative units. Rather than suppressing regional movements, India generally tried to address them through dialogue and constitutional means — as seen in the creation of new states like Nagaland, Meghalaya, and later Jharkhand, Uttarakhand, and Chhattisgarh. This approach helped channel regional aspirations through democratic institutions, strengthening national unity.
questions.chapter: क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाएँ / Regional Aspirations
questions.topic: Regional aspirations, federalism, linguistic reorganisation

questions.text:
(क) भारत और बांग्लादेश के बीच सम्बन्धों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) नेपाल में राजशाही से लोकतंत्र में परिवर्तित होने की प्रक्रिया का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Analyse the relations between India and Bangladesh.
OR
(b) Analyse the process of transition from monarchy to democracy in Nepal.

sub_questions.text: भारत और बांग्लादेश के बीच सम्बन्धों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the relations between India and Bangladesh.

key_points: Historical context: India played a key role in the liberation of Bangladesh in 1971
Areas of cooperation: trade, connectivity, water sharing, counter-terrorism
Areas of tension: illegal migration, sharing of river waters (Teesta), border disputes
Recent improvement in relations and strategic partnership

sub_questions.solution: India-Bangladesh relations have been both cooperative and complex. India played a decisive role in the liberation of Bangladesh from Pakistan in 1971, laying the foundation of a close bilateral bond. The two countries share extensive economic and cultural ties, with India being one of Bangladesh's largest trading partners. There is cooperation in areas of connectivity, energy, and counter-terrorism. However, tensions persist over the sharing of river waters — particularly the Teesta river dispute — illegal migration of Bangladeshis into India, and unresolved border demarcation issues. In recent years, both countries have worked to strengthen relations through high-level diplomatic visits, agreements on border management, and infrastructure development, making the partnership an important pillar of India's 'Neighbourhood First' policy.

sub_questions.text: नेपाल में राजशाही से लोकतंत्र में परिवर्तित होने की प्रक्रिया का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the process of transition from monarchy to democracy in Nepal.

key_points: Nepal was under absolute monarchy for long; political parties demanded democracy
1990: Pro-democracy movement led to constitutional monarchy and multiparty democracy
Maoist insurgency (1996-2006) destabilised the country
2006: Comprehensive Peace Agreement signed; monarchy abolished in 2008 and Nepal became a federal democratic republic

sub_questions.solution: Nepal's transition from monarchy to democracy was a long and turbulent process. Nepal was under a hereditary monarchy for centuries, with the king exercising absolute power. In 1990, a popular movement (People's Movement or Jana Andolan) forced King Birendra to accept a new constitution that established a constitutional monarchy with multiparty democracy. However, political instability continued, and in 1996, the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) launched an armed insurgency that lasted a decade. In 2001, a royal massacre led to political uncertainty. In 2006, a second People's Movement forced King Gyanendra to restore parliament, and a Comprehensive Peace Agreement ended the Maoist insurgency. In 2008, the Constituent Assembly formally abolished the monarchy and declared Nepal a federal democratic republic, completing the historic transition.

questions.solution: This question has an internal choice. See sub_questions (a) and (b) for full model answers.
questions.chapter: भारत के पड़ोसी देश / South Asia
questions.topic: India-Bangladesh relations; Nepal's democratic transition

questions.text: अपनी सुरक्षा को सुदृढ़ करने में भारत की रणनीति की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain India's strategy to strengthen its security.

key_points: Military modernisation and development of nuclear deterrence
Strengthening international alliances and bilateral security agreements
Addressing internal security threats through democratic and developmental means
Participation in UN peacekeeping missions and multilateral security cooperation

questions.solution: India's strategy to strengthen its security operates on multiple levels. First, India has pursued military modernisation by upgrading its armed forces, developing indigenous defence technology, and maintaining a credible nuclear deterrent based on the principle of 'No First Use.' Second, India has forged strategic partnerships with major powers such as the United States, Russia, France, and Israel to access advanced military technology and intelligence sharing. Third, India has addressed internal security threats — including insurgencies in the Northeast, the Kashmir conflict, and left-wing extremism — through a combination of military operations and political dialogue, development initiatives, and democratic accommodation. Fourth, India actively participates in UN peacekeeping missions and regional security forums like SAARC, SCO, and BIMSTEC to build a cooperative security environment. This multi-pronged strategy reflects India's understanding that security encompasses both external and internal dimensions.
questions.chapter: समकालीन विश्व में सुरक्षा / Security in the Contemporary World
questions.topic: India's security strategy, nuclear deterrence, internal security

questions.text: एक महत्वपूर्ण संसाधन के रूप में 'जल' के उदाहरण की सहायता से संसाधनों की भू-राजनीति की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the geo-politics of resources with the help of the example of 'water' as a crucial resource.

key_points: Geopolitics of resources means the political and strategic competition over access to and control of natural resources
Water is a finite, unevenly distributed, and vital resource — making it a source of inter-state tensions
Examples: disputes over rivers like the Nile, Mekong, Indus; India-Pakistan Indus Waters Treaty; India-Bangladesh Farakka barrage issue
Future 'water wars' are predicted; water scarcity drives migration, conflict, and diplomatic negotiations

questions.solution: The geopolitics of resources refers to the way in which competition over vital natural resources shapes the political relationships between nations. Water is among the most critical resources because it is essential for life, agriculture, and industry, yet its distribution is highly unequal across the globe. Many countries share river basins, making water a frequent source of inter-state tension. For instance, India and Pakistan have managed disputes over the Indus river system through the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960, though tensions persist. Similarly, India and Bangladesh have long negotiated over the sharing of the Ganga waters at Farakka. On a global level, countries dependent on the Nile and Mekong rivers compete fiercely for water access. As climate change intensifies water scarcity, experts warn that future conflicts may increasingly be driven by competition over water, making it a key dimension of 21st-century geopolitics.
questions.chapter: पर्यावरण और प्राकृतिक संसाधन / Environment and Natural Resources
questions.topic: Geopolitics of resources, water disputes, river treaties

questions.text:
(क) 1969 में काँग्रेस पार्टी को विभाजन की ओर ले जाने वाली किन्हीं दो घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) भारत से गरीबी हटाने के लिए इन्दिरा गाँधी द्वारा उठाए गए किन्हीं चार कदमों का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any two events that led to the split in the Congress Party in 1969.
OR
(b) Describe any four steps taken by Indira Gandhi to eradicate poverty (Garibi Hatao) in India.

sub_questions.text: 1969 में काँग्रेस पार्टी को विभाजन की ओर ले जाने वाली किन्हीं दो घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any two events that led to the split in the Congress Party in 1969.

key_points: The Presidential election of 1969 where Indira Gandhi supported V.V. Giri against the official Congress candidate Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
Nationalisation of 14 major banks in July 1969 against the wishes of the Syndicate

sub_questions.solution: Two key events led to the split in the Congress Party in 1969. The first was the Presidential election controversy of 1969. The Congress Syndicate — the group of powerful party bosses — nominated Neelam Sanjiva Reddy as the official presidential candidate. However, Indira Gandhi openly defied the Syndicate and supported V.V. Giri as an independent candidate. When Giri won, it was a direct challenge to the Syndicate's authority and deepened the rift within the party. The second event was the nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks in July 1969. Indira Gandhi announced this bold policy without consulting the Syndicate, using it as a populist measure to appeal to the poor. This action went against the Syndicate's conservative economic views and represented an open ideological break, ultimately leading to the formal split of Congress into Congress (I) and Congress (O).

sub_questions.text: भारत से गरीबी हटाने के लिए इन्दिरा गाँधी द्वारा उठाए गए किन्हीं चार कदमों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four steps taken by Indira Gandhi to eradicate poverty (Garibi Hatao) in India.

key_points: Nationalisation of 14 major banks in 1969 to direct credit to the poor and agriculture
Abolition of Privy Purses to former princes — ending financial privileges of royalty
Land reforms and ceiling on land ownership to redistribute land to the landless
Green Revolution support and expansion of public distribution system for food security

sub_questions.solution: Indira Gandhi took several steps under her 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty) campaign. First, she nationalised 14 major commercial banks in 1969, which made credit accessible to farmers, small businesses, and the poor by directing bank lending toward priority sectors. Second, she abolished the Privy Purses of former princely states in 1971, ending the constitutionally guaranteed payments to former rulers and redirecting resources toward public welfare. Third, she promoted land reforms including implementing land ceiling laws so that surplus land could be redistributed to landless farmers and agricultural labourers. Fourth, she expanded the Public Distribution System (PDS) and supported the Green Revolution by providing subsidies on seeds, fertilisers, and irrigation to boost agricultural production and ensure food security for the poor.

questions.solution: This question has an internal choice. See sub_questions (a) and (b) for full model answers.

questions.topic: Congress split 1969, Indira Gandhi, Garibi Hatao

questions.text: भारत की राष्ट्रीय एकता और अखंडता को मजबूत करने के लिए कोई दो कदम सुझाइए।
questions.text_english: Suggest any two steps to strengthen the national integration and unity of India.

key_points: Promoting inclusive development and reducing regional economic disparities to address the root causes of separatism
Strengthening constitutional institutions and promoting the values of secularism, democratic pluralism, and mutual respect among all communities

questions.solution: Two effective steps to strengthen national integration and unity in India are: First, promoting inclusive and balanced regional development so that no part of the country feels economically neglected or marginalised. Disparities in development often fuel regionalism and secessionist movements. Special packages, infrastructure investment, and employment generation in backward areas can reduce these grievances and strengthen people's faith in the Indian state. Second, reinforcing constitutional values of secularism, federalism, and democratic pluralism through education and public discourse. Teaching citizens about the importance of diversity and mutual respect, and ensuring that political leaders and institutions uphold these values, can help build a cohesive national identity while respecting the country's enormous cultural diversity.
questions.chapter: क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाएँ / Regional Aspirations
questions.topic: National integration, unity in diversity, federalism

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अवतरण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और इस पर आधारित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :

"आज़ादी के बाद पहली बार ऐसा हुआ कि काँग्रेस पार्टी लोक सभा का चुनाव हार गई। काँग्रेस को लोक सभा में केवल 154 सीटें मिली थीं। लोक सभा में जनता पार्टी और इसके साथी दलों को 330 सीटें मिलीं। उत्तर भारत में चुनावी माहौल काँग्रेस के एकदम खिलाफ था। काँग्रेस बिहार, उत्तर प्रदेश, दिल्ली, हरियाणा और पंजाब से एक भी सीट प्राप्त नहीं कर सकी।"
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on it :

"For the first time since independence, the Congress Party was defeated in the Lok Sabha elections. The Congress could win only 154 seats in the Lok Sabha. The Janata Party and its allies won 330 seats in the Lok Sabha. It was a massive electoral wave against the Congress in North India. The Congress lost in every constituency in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana and Punjab."
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित अवतरण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और इस पर आधारित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on it

sub_questions.text: उपर्युक्त अवतरण में लोक सभा के कौन-से आम चुनावों का जिक्र है ?
sub_questions.text_english: The above passage refers to which general elections to the Lok Sabha ?
sub_questions.solution: The passage describes the 1977 general elections, which were the 6th Lok Sabha elections, where the Congress was defeated for the first time after independence. However, based on CBSE answer key, the correct answer is (D) 7th. The passage refers to the elections post-Emergency (1977), which are the 6th general elections. Checking: the 1977 elections are the 6th Lok Sabha elections. The answer is (C) 6th. The Janata Party's victory in 1977 was indeed the 6th Lok Sabha election. The correct answer is (C) 6th.

sub_questions.text: लोक सभा की कुल कितनी सीटों के लिए चुनाव करवाया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: For how many total seats of the Lok Sabha are the elections held ?
sub_questions.solution: The Lok Sabha has a total of 543 elected seats (constituencies) for which elections are held. In addition, the President can nominate 2 members from the Anglo-Indian community (though this provision was abolished in 2020), making the total strength 545. However, elections are held for 543 seats. Option (D) 543 is correct.

sub_questions.text: जनता पार्टी की जीत के बाद निम्नलिखित में से कौन भारत के उप-प्रधान मंत्री थे ?
sub_questions.text_english: Who among the following was the Deputy Prime Minister of India after the victory of the Janata Party ?
sub_questions.solution: After the Janata Party's victory in 1977, Morarji Desai became the Prime Minister and Chaudhary Charan Singh became the Deputy Prime Minister. Charan Singh represented the peasant community and the Lok Dal faction within the Janata coalition. Atal Bihari Vajpayee served as External Affairs Minister and L.K. Advani as Information and Broadcasting Minister. Chandra Shekhar was president of the Janata Party. Hence option (A) Ch. Charan Singh is correct.

sub_questions.text: उस राज्य का नाम लिखिए जहाँ से उपर्युक्त चुनावों में काँग्रेस पार्टी केवल एक सीट ही जीत पाई थी।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the state from where the Congress Party could win only one seat in the above said elections.
sub_questions.solution: In the 1977 Lok Sabha elections, Congress was completely wiped out in the northern states mentioned in the passage. However, West Bengal, where the Left Front was the dominant force, was not part of the anti-Congress Janata wave and Congress managed to win only one seat from there. Option (B) West Bengal is correct.

questions.text:
भारत के दिए गए राजनीतिक रेखा-मानचित्र (पृष्ठ 13 पर), में चार राज्यों को (A), (B), (C) और (D) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है। नीचे दी गई जानकारी के आधार पर, इन राज्यों की पहचान कीजिए और अपनी उत्तर-पुस्तिका में इनके सही नाम, प्रयोग की गई जानकारी की क्रम संख्या तथा मानचित्र में दिया गया संबंधित अक्षर, नीचे दी गई तालिका के रूप में लिखिए :
(i) महाराजा बोधचन्द्र सिंह से सम्बन्धित राज्य
(ii) 1966 में बनाया गया राज्य
(iii) वह राज्य जो पहले मध्य प्रदेश का एक भाग था
(iv) जून 2014 में बनाया गया राज्य
questions.text_english:
In the given political outline map of India (on page 15), four States have been marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify these States on the basis of the information given below and write their correct names in your answer-book along with the respective serial number of the information used and the concerned alphabets given in the map :
(i) The State to which Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh belonged
(ii) The State which was created in 1966
(iii) The State which earlier was a part of Madhya Pradesh
(iv) The State which was created in June 2014

key_points: (i) Manipur — Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh was the ruler of Manipur who signed the Instrument of Accession; marked as D on the map (northeastern India)
(ii) Haryana — created in 1966 when Punjab was reorganised on linguistic lines; marked as C on the map
(iii) Chhattisgarh — carved out of Madhya Pradesh in November 2000; marked as B on the map
(iv) Telangana — created in June 2014 from Andhra Pradesh (note: carved from AP not MP, but the clue references a state created in June 2014); marked as A on the map

questions.solution: Based on the clues provided and the position of the marked states on the map: (i) Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh belonged to Manipur, which is in northeastern India and is marked as D on the map. He was the ruler who signed the Instrument of Accession joining India in 1949. (ii) Haryana was created in 1966 when the state of Punjab was reorganised on linguistic basis, separating Punjabi-speaking and Hindi-speaking areas; it is marked as C on the map. (iii) Chhattisgarh was part of Madhya Pradesh before being carved out as a separate state in November 2000; it is marked as B on the map. (iv) Telangana was created in June 2014 from the state of Andhra Pradesh; it is marked as A on the map.
questions.chapter: राष्ट्र निर्माण की चुनौतियाँ / Challenges of Nation Building
questions.topic: Formation of states, linguistic reorganisation, new states

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए कार्टून का अध्ययन कीजिए और इस पर आधारित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :
(कार्टून में एक साइकिल दिखाई गई है जिसके फ्रेम पर 'चीन' लिखा है। साइकिल के पिछले पहिये में डॉलर का चिह्न बना हुआ है।)
questions.text_english:
Study the cartoon given below and answer the questions based on it :
(The cartoon shows a bicycle with 'CHINA' written on the frame. The rear wheel of the bicycle has a dollar symbol on it.)

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा वैध कारण चीन का प्रतिनिधित्व करने के लिए 'साइकिल' को चुनने के लिए सही है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the valid reason to choose 'cycle' to represent China ?

options.A: साइकिल का प्रयोग करने में चीन विश्व का सबसे अग्रणी देश है।
options.B: यह चीन की कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी का प्रतीक चिह्न है।
options.C: यह चीन की गरीबी को दर्शाती है।
options.D: चीन में साइकिल चलाना एक लोकप्रिय खेल है।

options_english.A: China is the largest user of cycles in the world.
options_english.B: It is the symbol of Communist Party of China.
options_english.D: Popularity of cycling as a sport in China.

sub_questions.solution: The cycle is used to represent China because China has historically been the world's largest user and manufacturer of bicycles. For decades, the bicycle was the primary mode of transportation for the Chinese population, symbolising China's vast working population and its economic character. Option (A) is correct.

sub_questions.text: साइकिल के पिछले पहिये में 'डालर' क्या दर्शाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What does the dollar in the rear wheel of the cycle depict ?

options.A: चीन पर अमरीकी अर्थव्यवस्था का प्रभाव
options.B: दोनों के बीच आधे-आधे की भागीदारी
options.C: चीन की अमरीकी अर्थव्यवस्था पर निर्भरता
options.D: अमरीका द्वारा चीन को दी गई आर्थिक सहायता

options_english.A: The influence of the US economy on China
options_english.B: Fifty percent partnership of the two
options_english.C: Dependence of China on US economy
options_english.D: Economic aid to China by US

sub_questions.solution: The dollar symbol in the rear wheel of the cycle represents the significant influence of the US economy on China. After China adopted its 'Open Door' policy under Deng Xiaoping in 1978, it opened up to foreign investment and began deep economic integration with the US. The dollar symbolises the American economic influence that has driven China's remarkable economic growth. Option (A) is correct.

sub_questions.text: चीन में प्रारम्भिक वर्षों में किस प्रकार की अर्थव्यवस्था थी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which form of economy was popular initially in China ?
sub_questions.solution: In the initial years after the Communist revolution of 1949, China followed a Socialist economy under Mao Zedong. The state controlled all means of production, collectivised agriculture, and followed central planning on the Soviet model. Private enterprise was abolished. It was only after 1978 that China began to gradually open its economy with market-oriented reforms. Option (C) Socialist is correct.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प कार्टून द्वारा दिए गए संदेश की सबसे सही अभिव्यक्ति है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following option is the most appropriate message given by the cartoon ?

options.A: चीन केवल अमरीकी अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए खुला है।
options.B: चीन ने अमरीका के साथ व्यापारिक सम्बन्ध स्थापित कर लिए हैं।
options.C: चीन केवल यूरोपीय देशों के साथ कार्य करता है।
options.D: चीन ने डालर को अपनी मुद्रा बना लिया है।

options_english.A: China is open only to US economy.
options_english.B: China has established trade relations with US.
options_english.C: China works only with European countries.
options_english.D: China has adopted dollar as its currency.

sub_questions.solution: The most appropriate message of the cartoon is that China has established trade and economic relations with the United States. The bicycle labelled 'China' with a dollar symbol on its wheel conveys that China's economic momentum is connected to its trade relationship with the US. It does not suggest China has abandoned its own currency or works only with the US — it simply shows the important economic partnership. Option (B) is correct.

questions.text:
(क) सोवियत संघ के विघटन के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं तीन कारणों की परख कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद भारत और रूस के बीच मैत्रीपूर्ण एवं सहयोगात्मक सम्बन्धों के किन्हीं तीन कारणों की परख कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Examine any three reasons responsible for the disintegration of the Soviet Union.
OR
(b) Examine any three reasons for the friendly and cooperative relations between India and Russia after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

sub_questions.text: सोवियत संघ के विघटन के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं तीन कारणों की परख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Examine any three reasons responsible for the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Economic stagnation and failure of the Soviet economic model
Political reforms under Gorbachev (Glasnost and Perestroika) which unleashed forces beyond state control
Rise of nationalist movements in Soviet republics seeking independence

sub_questions.solution: Three important reasons for the disintegration of the Soviet Union are: First, the Soviet economy suffered from deep structural weaknesses. The centralised command economy was inefficient, unable to satisfy consumer demands, and could not compete with the West technologically. Massive military expenditure during the Cold War drained resources, leading to economic stagnation. Second, Mikhail Gorbachev's reform policies of Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring) in the late 1980s, while intended to revitalise the system, had unintended consequences. Political openness allowed public criticism of the Communist Party and the government, weakening the ideological legitimacy of Soviet rule. Third, nationalist and separatist movements intensified across Soviet republics. Many republics — the Baltic states (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania), Ukraine, and others — began demanding independence, arguing for self-determination. The Soviet state proved unable to suppress these movements by force without international condemnation, and the centre could not hold. These three forces together led to the formal dissolution of the USSR on December 25, 1991.

sub_questions.text: सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद भारत और रूस के बीच मैत्रीपूर्ण एवं सहयोगात्मक सम्बन्धों के किन्हीं तीन कारणों की परख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Examine any three reasons for the friendly and cooperative relations between India and Russia after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Long historical friendship and strategic partnership dating back to the Soviet era
Defence and military cooperation — Russia is a major supplier of arms and defence technology to India
Convergence of interests on issues like multipolarity, terrorism, and opposition to US unilateralism

sub_questions.solution: Three key reasons for the friendly and cooperative relations between India and Russia after the Soviet disintegration are: First, both countries share a deep historical friendship. The relationship between India and the Soviet Union was built over decades of cooperation in defence, industry, and diplomacy, including the 1971 Treaty of Friendship. This legacy of trust carried forward into Russia-India relations, providing a strong foundation for cooperation in the post-Cold War era. Second, Russia remains India's most important defence partner, supplying advanced military hardware such as fighter aircraft, submarines, tanks, and missile systems. Defence collaboration is a cornerstone of their bilateral relationship, with joint ventures in missile development such as the BrahMos programme. Third, both countries share strategic interests in building a multipolar world order and opposing unilateralism. They work together in multilateral forums like BRICS, SCO, and the UN, advocating for reforms in global governance and greater representation for developing nations. These shared interests make India-Russia relations naturally cooperative even in the changed post-Soviet world.

questions.solution: This question has an internal choice. See sub_questions (a) and (b) for full model answers.
questions.chapter: शीत युद्ध का दौर / The Cold War Era
questions.topic: Disintegration of Soviet Union, India-Russia relations

questions.text:
(क) किन्हीं तीन तर्कों की सहायता से वर्तमान विश्व में संयुक्त राष्ट्र के महत्त्व की व्याख्या कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद् के संगठन एवं कार्यों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the importance of the United Nations in the present day world with the help of any three arguments.
OR
(b) Explain the composition and functions of the UN Security Council.

sub_questions.text: किन्हीं तीन तर्कों की सहायता से वर्तमान विश्व में संयुक्त राष्ट्र के महत्त्व की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the importance of the United Nations in the present day world with the help of any three arguments.

key_points: The UN provides a platform for peaceful resolution of international disputes and conflict prevention
The UN coordinates humanitarian assistance, development aid, and responses to global crises
The UN promotes human rights, international law, and global norms through its various agencies and conventions

sub_questions.solution: The United Nations remains a vital institution in the contemporary world for several reasons. First, the UN serves as the primary platform for the peaceful resolution of disputes between nations. Through mechanisms like the Security Council, the International Court of Justice, and diplomatic negotiations, the UN helps prevent conflicts from escalating into full-scale wars. It has successfully mediated numerous crises and continues to deploy peacekeeping forces in conflict zones across the globe, from Congo to Lebanon. Second, the UN coordinates the international response to global crises — whether humanitarian disasters caused by wars and natural calamities, development challenges, or health emergencies. UN agencies like UNICEF, UNHCR, WHO, and the World Food Programme provide critical assistance to millions of people. Third, the UN has established a framework of international law and human rights norms through documents like the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), various conventions on genocide, refugees, and the rights of women and children. These norms hold states accountable and help build a rules-based international order. These functions make the UN indispensable in the current world.

sub_questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद् के संगठन एवं कार्यों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the composition and functions of the UN Security Council.

key_points: Composition: 15 members — 5 permanent (P5: USA, UK, France, Russia, China) with veto power, and 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms
Function: Maintaining international peace and security
Function: Authorising peacekeeping operations and imposing sanctions
Function: Recommending the appointment of the Secretary-General and admission of new UN members

sub_questions.solution: The UN Security Council is the principal organ responsible for international peace and security. In terms of composition, it has 15 members: 5 permanent members — the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China — who hold the right of veto, meaning that any one of them can block a resolution. The remaining 10 seats are held by non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms on a regional rotation basis. Regarding functions, the Security Council investigates disputes that may threaten international peace and recommends methods of resolving them. It has the authority to impose economic sanctions and authorise the use of collective military force against aggressors. The Council also directs UN peacekeeping missions. Additionally, it recommends candidates for the post of Secretary-General to the General Assembly and plays a role in approving new UN member states. Decisions on substantive matters require nine affirmative votes with no permanent member casting a veto.

questions.text:
(क) भारतीय विदेश नीति की किन्हीं तीन महत्त्वपूर्ण विशेषताओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) 1971 के भारत-पाकिस्तान युद्ध के ठीक पहले और बाद की किन्हीं तीन महत्त्वपूर्ण घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any three important features of India's Foreign Policy.
OR
(b) Describe any three important events just before and after the India-Pakistan war in 1971.

sub_questions.text: भारतीय विदेश नीति की किन्हीं तीन महत्त्वपूर्ण विशेषताओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any three important features of India's Foreign Policy.

key_points: Non-alignment: refusing to join any military bloc during the Cold War and maintaining strategic autonomy
Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence): mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality, and peaceful coexistence
Support for decolonisation and opposition to imperialism; leadership in the Non-Aligned Movement

sub_questions.solution: India's foreign policy since independence has been guided by several distinctive principles. The first and most defining feature is Non-Alignment. During the Cold War, India refused to become a member of either the US-led NATO or the Soviet-led Warsaw Pact, choosing instead to maintain strategic autonomy and pursue an independent foreign policy based on national interest. India became a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement. The second key feature is Panchsheel, the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence agreed upon by India and China in 1954 — mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference in internal affairs, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. These became foundational to India's approach to international relations. The third feature is India's commitment to anti-colonialism and support for decolonisation movements across Asia and Africa. India used international forums like the United Nations to oppose imperialism, apartheid in South Africa, and racial discrimination, reflecting its own experience as a former colony.

sub_questions.text: 1971 के भारत-पाकिस्तान युद्ध के ठीक पहले और बाद की किन्हीं तीन महत्त्वपूर्ण घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any three important events just before and after the India-Pakistan war in 1971.

key_points: Before the war: Pakistani military crackdown in East Pakistan (March 1971) and massive refugee influx into India
Before/during: India signed the Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation (August 1971) to deter US and Chinese intervention
After the war: surrender of Pakistani forces and creation of Bangladesh (December 16, 1971), followed by the Simla Agreement of 1972 between India and Pakistan

sub_questions.solution: Three important events just before and after the 1971 India-Pakistan war are: First, in March 1971, the Pakistani military launched a brutal crackdown on the people of East Pakistan (Operation Searchlight), targeting Bengali civilians, intellectuals, and Hindu minorities. This triggered a massive refugee crisis, with nearly ten million people fleeing into India, creating enormous political, economic, and humanitarian pressure on the Indian government to intervene. Second, in August 1971, India signed the Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation. This treaty, while not a formal military alliance, provided India with a strategic deterrent — it signalled that the Soviet Union would prevent any escalation by the US or China if India went to war to help Bangladesh gain independence. Third, after the 13-day war in December 1971, Pakistani forces surrendered on December 16 — the largest military surrender since World War II — and Bangladesh was born as an independent nation. Subsequently, in July 1972, India and Pakistan signed the Simla Agreement, under which both countries agreed to settle future disputes bilaterally and India returned the prisoners of war.

(क) 1988 से 1993 के बीच भारत में घटी किन्हीं चार राजनीतिक घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) 1989 से 2004 तक के 'गठबंधन सरकारों के युग' के किन्हीं चार परिणामों का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any four political developments in India that took place between 1988 to 1993.
OR
(b) Describe any four consequences of the 'Era of Coalition governments' starting from 1989 to 2004.

sub_questions.text: 1988 से 1993 के बीच भारत में घटी किन्हीं चार राजनीतिक घटनाओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four political developments in India that took place between 1988 to 1993.

key_points: 1989 general elections: Congress lost; VP Singh became PM heading the National Front government supported by BJP and Left
1990: Mandal Commission controversy — VP Singh's government announced implementation of OBC reservations, leading to widespread protests
1991: Assassination of Rajiv Gandhi; Congress won mid-term elections and PV Narasimha Rao became PM; LPG economic reforms launched
1992: Demolition of Babri Masjid on December 6 triggered communal riots across India

sub_questions.solution: Four important political developments in India between 1988 and 1993 are: First, the 1989 general elections resulted in the defeat of Rajiv Gandhi's Congress. VP Singh's Janata Dal-led National Front formed a minority government with outside support from the BJP and the Left parties. This marked the beginning of coalition politics at the national level. Second, in 1990, VP Singh's government announced the implementation of the Mandal Commission report, recommending 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central government jobs. This triggered violent protests from upper-caste groups and deepened caste-based political mobilisation. Third, in May 1991, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by an LTTE suicide bomber during an election campaign in Tamil Nadu. Despite this tragedy, Congress won the elections and PV Narasimha Rao became Prime Minister, launching landmark economic liberalisation reforms in July 1991. Fourth, in December 1992, the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya was demolished by a large Hindu mob, triggering widespread communal riots across India that killed thousands and created one of the most serious communal crises in post-independence history.

sub_questions.text: 1989 से 2004 तक के 'गठबंधन सरकारों के युग' के किन्हीं चार परिणामों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four consequences of the 'Era of Coalition governments' starting from 1989 to 2004.

key_points: Political instability: frequent elections and short-lived governments leading to policy uncertainty
Rise of regional parties: coalition compulsions gave regional parties disproportionate influence
Policy changes due to coalition pressures: government policies shaped more by coalition management than national interest
Strengthening of federalism: states and regional parties gained more bargaining power in national politics

sub_questions.solution: Four significant consequences of the era of coalition governments from 1989 to 2004 are: First, political instability became a defining feature of this period. India witnessed several short-lived governments — including those of VP Singh, Chandra Shekhar, HD Deve Gowda, and IK Gujral — which could not complete their terms. Frequent elections drained resources and created uncertainty in policy-making. Second, regional parties gained unprecedented influence. Since no single party commanded a majority, regional parties like the Samajwadi Party, BSP, Telugu Desam Party, and DMK became crucial coalition partners and could extract significant concessions from the central government on state-specific issues. Third, policy-making often became hostage to coalition compulsions. Governments had to accommodate the demands of diverse alliance partners, making it difficult to push through bold reforms in areas like economic policy, labour laws, or national security. Fourth, this era paradoxically also strengthened Indian federalism. States gained more fiscal resources, greater autonomy, and a stronger voice in national affairs. The 73rd and 74th constitutional amendments deepening grassroots democracy, and the economic liberalisation that decentralised some economic decision-making, helped strengthen federal dynamics during this period.
